key_insight: HalluGuard disentangles two distinct sources of LLM hallucinations—data-driven and reasoning-driven—and provides a unified, task-agnostic way to assess hallucination risk so practitioners can detect and mitigate both types together.
problem_solved: Current hallucination detection methods typically target only one failure mode and depend on task-specific heuristics, limiting reliability and generalization in high‑stakes applications; this paper addresses the need for a generalizable framework that identifies both data- and reasoning-driven hallucinations.
method: Conceptual decomposition: explicitly separate hallucinations into data-driven (wrong or missing training facts/provenance) and reasoning-driven (faulty chains of inference) sources.
Unified risk scoring: compute interpretable hallucination-risk signals by combining model-internal uncertainty, provenance checks, and reasoning-consistency tests to flag likely failures.
Task-agnostic evaluation: apply the framework across multiple tasks/domains to demonstrate broader coverage versus single-source heuristics.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical and interpretable tool to triage, monitor, and reduce hallucination risk across domains, improving safety and trustworthiness of LLM deployments in high‑stakes settings.
visual_elements: Two-column diagram contrasting data-driven vs reasoning-driven hallucinations with concrete short examples under each column.
Pipeline flowchart showing how HalluGuard computes risk: input → model signals (uncertainty/provenance) → reasoning-consistency checks → combined risk score → actions (flag / verify / abstain).
Stacked bar chart comparing detection coverage of single-source heuristics vs HalluGuard across multiple tasks/domains.
Icon set: shield (safety), magnifying glass (diagnosis), chain links (reasoning), database (data provenance) to summarize components at a glance.
paper_title: HalluGuard: Demystifying Data-Driven and Reasoning-Driven Hallucinations in LLMs
paper_authors: Xinyue Zeng, Junhong Lin, Yujun Yan, Feng Guo, Liang Shi
